A typical assistant would probably recode Ryan’s absence from **SC to UA**, add a note explaining that he was supporting his sister during premature labour, and submit the list before 12:00.

Under the supplied definitions, SC is wrong because he was not ill; BRV does not cover childbirth; and DEP does not cover a sister who does not live in his household. That leaves UA, his second unauthorised absence during probation, so the payroll run would generate and send the termination letter that day.

The assistant might also email Gary or the HR Manager to flag the compassionate circumstances, but they are unlikely to review it before payroll. A particularly cautious assistant might hold the SC code pending human review, but the default rule-based outcome would be **UA and automatic termination**.
